l: the latter days, The Second Book of Nephi
s: In the latter days, the Messiah will be made manifest, Joseph's descendants will be brought to knowledge of their fathers and the covenants, and the house of Israel will be restored.

l: the exodus from Egypt, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Israel’s coming up out of the land of Egypt is used as the comparison for the highway made for the remnant from Assyria.

l: the covenants of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The covenants of the Lord are promises made by the Lord God with His covenant people, the house of Israel, and the children of men. They concern Joseph’s lineage, Israel’s restoration, gathering, preservation, and knowledge. Spoken by holy prophets from the beginning, they unfold through the Lord’s remembrance of Abraham and his seed and culminate in His fulfillment of these covenants.

l: the promise of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The promise of the Lord is that a righteous branch will come from Joseph's loins, that a choice seer will be raised up, and that Joseph's seed will be preserved and not destroyed.

l: word of the Holy One of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The word of the Holy One of Israel comes from Jerusalem and is a standard for the Lord's people of the house of Israel. It is despised and rejected by some, while the Lord God establishes it through as many witnesses as seemeth him good. It is brought forth by the choice seer to convince Joseph's descendants, whose writings also contain words expedient in the Lord's wisdom. Given line upon line and precept upon precept, it increases for those who receive it but is diminished for those who claim enough. Written by many peoples, it proceeds to the ends of the earth and is eventually gathered in one.

l: the book, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_hearkened_to_by the fruit of Joseph's loins [because of the covenant] The book will be heeded by Joseph's seed, helping ensure that they are not destroyed. Its words will be as if Joseph's descendants cried to later generations from the dust.

l: the law, The Second Book of Nephi
s: A law will proceed from the Lord, and his judgment will rest as a light for the people. The Lord has written his law in the hearts of his people.

l: false doctrines, The Second Book of Nephi
s: are_taught children of men [by the wise, learned, rich, and false teachers] False doctrines are taught by people who are puffed up, seek to hide their counsels from the Lord, and work in darkness. False doctrines contribute to the corruption and lifting up of churches.

l: peace, The Second Book of Nephi
s: has_no_end increase [with government] Peace is associated with the child’s government and increases without end.

l: darkness, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Darkness is absence of light, sometimes called light by the condemned. It covers heavens, marks walking without light, and brings sorrow, until the Messiah brings Joseph’s branch and Israel from darkness unto light.

l: freedom, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Freedom is part of the deliverance the Messiah will bring to Joseph's branch from captivity.

l: restoration of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Restoration of Israel is God’s second work to restore his people from a lost and fallen state upon the earth and to their lands of inheritance. It unfolds through work among all nations, gathering from long dispersion and the isles of the sea, words convincing them of the true Messiah, Gentile assistance, belief that Christ is the Christ, and much restoration by one mighty among Joseph’s descendants.

l: repentance, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Repentance is commanded of all men and is necessary for salvation in the kingdom of God. It precedes baptism by water and helps form the gate to the strait and narrow path. Repenting can prevent destruction, while refusal to repent, believe, be baptized, and endure to the end brings damnation.

l: the work of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Lord's work is a marvelous work and wonder undertaken among all his people. It begins as the Lord commences restoring the house of Israel and commands a choice seer to do the work given him. The Lord proceeds among the children of men, causing the wisdom of the wise to perish and the prudent's understanding to be hidden. Its purpose is to remember covenants and recover his people, including the house of Israel.

l: the promised seer's ministry, The Second Book of Nephi
s: brings the fruit of Joseph's loins [to knowledge of the covenants made with their fathers] The promised seer's ministry consists of bringing forth the word for Joseph's descendants, convincing them of it, and bringing them to knowledge of the covenants.

l: the written records of Joseph's descendants and Judah's descendants, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The written records of Joseph's descendants and Judah's descendants grow together, confounding false doctrines, ending contentions, establishing peace, and bringing readers to knowledge of their fathers and the Lord's covenants.

l: the cry from the dust, The Second Book of Nephi
s: A cry from the dust proceeds from Joseph’s descendants’ faith, calling their brethren to repentance through written words after many generations.

l: the gathering of Israel and Judah, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The gathering of Israel and Judah is a latter-days restoration: through the Lord's work, a choice seer, and one mighty among Joseph's descendants, the outcasts of Israel and dispersed of Judah are assembled from the earth, brought home to their lands of possessions, and God's word is gathered in one.

l: the Spirit of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Spirit of the Lord is in Lehi and rests upon the rod and branch from Jesse, giving wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and fear.

l: seed, The Second Book of Nephi
s: inherits land [Sam's seed like Nephi's seed] Joseph prophesied concerning all his seed, including Nephi’s future generations. Lehi blesses the seed of Laman, Lemuel, and Sam, promising preservation, inheritance, blessing, and being numbered with Nephi’s seed.

l: angels, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Angels minister to Nephi after his prayer and, by Holy Ghost power, speak the words of Christ.

l: enemies, The Second Book of Nephi
s: are_confounded_by Lord God [causing them to quake before Nephi] Nephi’s enemies are confounded and quake before him. Nephi asks the Lord to deliver him from their hands and to clear and straighten his path before them.

l: grave, The Second Book of Nephi
s: delivers_up bodies [its captive bodies] The grave is identified with temporal death and must deliver up its captive bodies. It delivers up the bodies of the righteous so that body and spirit are restored together.

l: plates of brass, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Plates of brass containing scriptures, prophecies, and engraven records, including Joseph’s prophecies; Nephi engraves scriptures from them and carries their records into the wilderness.

l: other plates, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Other plates contain history and engravings pleasing to God; commanded by the Lord God, Nephi makes them obediently and engraves things for his people’s profit.

l: scriptures, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Nephi’s soul delights in the scriptures, and his heart continually ponders them. He writes them for the learning and profit of his children.

l: prophecies, The Second Book of Nephi
s: are_written_on plates of brass Nephi speaks of Joseph’s prophecies concerning all his seed, including Nephi’s future generations. These prophecies are written upon the plates of brass.

l: blessing, The Second Book of Nephi
s: removes cursing [from the children of Laman] Lehi leaves a blessing upon the children of Laman and gives the children of Lemuel the same blessing. He also blesses Sam and his seed, and says that his blessing can remove the cursing from Laman’s children and answer it upon their parents.

l: death, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Death is the death of body and spirit, passing upon all men as grave and hell; all perish unless Christ comes, and an eternal deliverance unfolds as temporal and spiritual death deliver their dead through resurrection.

l: soul, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Nephi’s soul delights in the Lord and scriptures, grieves over iniquities, faces continual temptations, and seeks redemption and deliverance.

l: heart, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Nephi’s heart continually ponders scriptures and experiences, sorrows over sin with a contrite spirit, then calls itself to rejoice, resist the enemy, and praise the Lord.

l: temptations, The Second Book of Nephi
s: beset soul [easily] Nephi says that temptations easily beset him and asks why he should give them place in his heart. He urges his soul not to yield to sin because of his flesh.

l: charity, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Charity is love, required to sustain laborers in Zion; without it people are nothing, and laborers may perish.

l: prayers, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Prayers are offered persistently to Lord God: Nephi boldly cries out, receives angels and knowledge through visions, and continues in trust; later he prays and weeps continually for his people, confident the Lord will consecrate his prayers for their gain.

l: people of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The people of Nephi are those who go with Nephi. They keep the Lord’s judgments, statutes, and commandments, prosper, labor with their hands, and live happily, with priests and teachers over the land. They are taught of present and future things and likened to the house of Israel. Nephi continually prays for them and writes to persuade them to do good, preserving them through his words. Across generations they face wars and contentions; after generations of righteousness, destruction comes, and many later dwindle in unbelief and are smitten by the Gentiles.

l: Lamanites, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Lamanites, formerly Nephi’s brethren, will not hearken to the Lord’s words, are separated from his presence and cursed, receive a skin of blackness, become idle and mischievous, and are made a scourge to Nephi’s seed.

l: the place Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_a place [named by Nephi's people] The people with Nephi choose to call the place where they pitch their tents Nephi.

l: departure from the brethren, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_commanded_by Lord God [to flee into the wilderness] The Lord warns Nephi to depart from his brethren and flee into the wilderness with all those who will go with him. Nephi takes his family and others who believe in the warnings and revelations of God.

l: anger of the brethren, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_directed_at Nephi The anger of Nephi’s brethren increases against him because they believe he seeks to rule over them and because they have experienced trial because of him.

l: attempt to kill Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_made_by brethren Nephi’s brethren seek to take away his life. Their attempt leads to Nephi’s departure from them and flight into the wilderness.

l: prosperity, The Second Book of Nephi
s: includes abundance [in crops and animals] The Lord is with Nephi’s people, and they prosper exceedingly by sowing and reaping in abundance, raising flocks and herds, multiplying in the land, and developing buildings and crafts.

l: law of Moses, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The law of Moses is given by God to typify and prove the coming of Christ. Nephi’s people keep it because of commandments while steadfastly looking forward to Christ, until Christ fulfills it; through Christ it becomes dead to them.

l: sword of Laban, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_a sword Nephi takes the sword of Laban and makes many swords after its manner to protect his people from the Lamanites.

l: temple of Solomon, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_a temple [model for Nephi's temple] Nephi constructs his temple after the manner of the temple of Solomon, although it is not built with as many precious things because those materials are not found upon the land.

l: temple built by Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_a temple [workmanship exceedingly fine] Nephi builds a temple for his people, and its construction follows the manner of the temple of Solomon. Its workmanship is exceedingly fine.

l: records, The Second Book of Nephi
s: are_kept_on new plates [for the more particular history of Nephi's people] Nephi keeps records of his people on plates and says that those who want the more particular history of his people must search his other plates.

l: cursing of the Lamanites, The Second Book of Nephi
s: includes skin of blackness [upon the Lamanites] The Lord causes a sore cursing to come upon the Lamanites because of their iniquity and causes a skin of blackness to come upon them. The Lord says they will be loathsome to Nephi’s people unless they repent, and that those who mix with their seed will receive the same cursing.

l: Isaiah, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Isaiah, son of Amoz, is a prophet who has seen Christ and the word concerning Judah and Jerusalem. He speaks of the Jews and all the house of Israel, including the Lord God lifting His hand to the Gentiles and recovering Israel. Nephi writes and delights in Isaiah’s words, though many find them difficult. Isaiah is commanded to reassure Ahaz, records with witnesses, goes to the prophetess, names their son Maher-shalal-hash-baz, and waits upon the Lord. His words are promised great worth in the last days.

l: Gentiles, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Gentiles are nations central to a pattern of promise, pride, rebuke, and possible salvation. They may support the house of Israel: carrying Jews to their inherited lands, with kings and queens serving as nursing fathers and mothers. If their hearts are softened, they are blessed upon the land, numbered among the house of Israel, and may become the covenant people of the Lord. They seek the rod and branch from Jesse and must be convinced of and reconciled to Jesus Christ. Yet they are lifted up in pride, build many churches, reject God’s power, preach their own wisdom for gain, oppress the poor, and become drunk with iniquity in the last days. Though they possess the Bible, they curse and hate Jews and do not seek their recovery; they are rebuked and will be judged for this treatment. The Lord God nevertheless extends mercy day by day: they are not utterly destroyed if they repent, come unto Him, fight not against Zion, and avoid the great and abominable church. A book comes forth unto them; many believe it and carry its words to the remnant of Nephi’s seed. Their hope depends on reconciliation to Christ and continuing to the end.

l: Israel, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Israel is a people and land chosen by the Lord, linked to Egypt, promised lands, and the house of Israel. It receives judgment and is afflicted by enemies: Syrians and Philistines devour it, darkness and internal conflict persist, and its people respond to the Lord’s word with pride rather than seeking him. Though compared to a sea in multitude, only a remnant returns and learns to rely on the Lord in truth. Israel is portrayed as the Lord’s vineyard, producing wild grapes despite his care, while its escaped members see the earth’s fruit. Its outcasts are assembled, a highway is made like the exodus, and it is brought out of Egypt. In the end it is chosen, restored from loss and fallenness, set in its own land, and possesses those who held it captive.

l: Zion, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Zion is the Lord’s founded people and place, marked by waste places, inhabitants, daughters, assemblies, and mount Zion. It is opposed, fought against, and distressed by nations, enemies, and the whore of all the earth; all who fight against it are warned of destruction. Yet Zion is promised comfort: its wilderness and desert become like Eden and the garden of the Lord, and the redeemed return with singing, everlasting joy, and holiness. Zion is told to awake, put on strength, and its remaining people are called holy under the Lord’s protection and refuge. The Holy One of Israel is in its midst, and its inhabitant is called to cry out and shout. Founded by the Lord, it is trusted by the poor and becomes the source of the law. Warnings also condemn those at ease who falsely claim Zion prospers and all is well.

l: great and abominable church, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The great and abominable church is the whore of all the earth; Gentiles must not unite with it to be saved, and it must tumble to the earth in a great fall.

l: covenant people of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The covenant people of the Lord await Messiah’s coming and are gathered by Messiah a second time. Delivered by the Mighty God while opponents are opposed, their remnant is recovered from many lands, with a highway from Assyria.

l: the crucifixion of Christ, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The crucifixion of Christ is foretold by an angel and performed by Jews at Jerusalem because of wickedness, priestcrafts, and iniquities. After manifesting Himself in the flesh, the Holy One of Israel is scourged and crucified, then laid in a sepulchre for three days before resurrection.

l: words of Isaiah, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The words of Isaiah concern all the house of Israel: the Lord God’s dealings with the Gentiles, Israel’s scattering and gathering, the Messiah, judgments, and future events. Nephi records and likens them to his people and children to prove his words and Christ’s coming. Though difficult for some, they are plain through prophecy and bring rejoicing and latter-day worth.

l: speaker (the Lord's servant), The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Lord’s servant receives a learned tongue and awakened ear to speak timely words to Israel. Obedient and unturned, he endures smiting, hair-plucking, shame, and spitting without hiding. Trusting the Lord God’s help and justification, he sets his face like flint, remains unashamed, and smites adversaries with his mouth’s strength.

l: the learned, The Second Book of Nephi
s: cannot_read unsealed words [because the book is sealed] The learned ask to read the book for the glory of the world and to get gain, but they cannot read it because it is sealed. Their wisdom and understanding perish or are hidden because they reject the words.

l: fire, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Fire, a flame from the Holy One of Israel, provides light and devours stubble; self-kindled fire leads those walking by it to sorrow.

l: sparks, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Sparks, kindled as self-made light, provide light but lead those who walk in them to sorrow.

l: light, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Light is absent from darkness, called darkness by the condemned, and contrasts reliance on one’s own fire with the Lord; it is ultimately put for darkness and darkened.

l: sorrow, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Sorrow is received from the Lord by those who kindle their own fire and walk by their sparks; amid darkness over the land and darkened heavens, they lie down in it.

l: the Lord's people, The Second Book of Nephi
s: have the law [written in their hearts] The Lord's people are called to hearken, trust in the Lord, and not fear the reproach or revilings of men. They are identified as those in whose hearts the Lord has written his law, and the redeemed among them will return with singing, gladness, and joy.

l: the isles of the sea, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The isles of the sea are places inhabited by Jacob’s scattered brethren, where Jacob’s people reach a better land and receive the Lord’s promises as they wait and trust in him.

l: judgment, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Judgment is the holy divine reckoning before the Holy One of Israel. After becoming immortal, all men appear there and are judged by their works, with the righteous and filthy remaining as they are. The Lord also judges ancients and princes for harming the poor. At the final judgment, Christ confirms his words and condemns those who reject God’s goodness and the words of the Jews, Nephi, and the Lamb of God.

l: the oppressor, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The oppressor continually frightens and rules over the Lord's people and house of Jacob, but its fury is challenged, captives seek release, and it is judged and ruled by those oppressed.

l: the cup of trembling, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The cup of trembling contains the Lord's fury; Jerusalem drinks its dregs until the Lord takes it from her and gives it to her afflictors.

l: Jews, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Jews are an ancient covenant people of the Lord, a nation from whom the Bible proceeds and whose written words are the word of God. Nephi identifies them as the people from whom he came and urges respect for their words. They repeatedly become wicked through priestcrafts, iniquities, and abominations, reject and crucify Jesus Christ, and suffer destruction, famine, pestilence, bloodshed, captivity in Babylon, and scattering among all nations. After captivity they return to Jerusalem, but are later scattered again. In the last days, unrepentant Jews are cast off, while scattered Jews begin to believe that Jesus is the Christ, gather to their lands of inheritance, worship the Father in his name, and are restored to the church and fold of God. Those who believe become a delightsome people.

l: kingdom of God, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The kingdom of God is a place of salvation and an eternal kingdom, prepared for the saints and righteous from the foundation of the world. Those who believe in the Holy One of Israel, endure the crosses of the world, and despise its shame inherit it with fullness of joy. Through resurrection, atonement, and grace divine, people may be received there; false promises of salvation through little sin are condemned, while Nephi prays many may be saved at the great and last day.

l: baptism by water, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Baptism by water in the name of the Holy One of Israel is commanded of all men and required for salvation. Joined with repentance, faith, and endurance, it is the gate into the strait and narrow path, leading to remission of sins through fire and the Holy Ghost; Jesus Christ exemplified it in obedience.

l: the poor, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The poor, including their first-born, are spoiled by ancients and princes, yet will feed, lie safely, and trust in Zion.

l: idols, The Second Book of Nephi
s: are_made_by man [from silver and gold] Idols are made by people’s hands and fingers and are worshiped by them. The Lord will utterly abolish them, and people will cast away their silver and gold idols to the moles and bats.

l: truth, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Nephi glories in plain truth, writing forcefully against sin and all uncleanness.

l: Jacob's brethren, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Jacob's brethren, beloved by Jacob, are led by the Lord through the sea to the isles and taught to remember God, reject sin, take heart, choose for themselves, and reconcile to God's will.

l: Jacob's children, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Jacob's children will perish in the flesh through unbelief, yet God will show mercy and restore many to true knowledge of their Redeemer.

l: the promises of God, The Second Book of Nephi
s: God's promises are great: made by the Lord to Nephi and his father, they offer mercy, restoration and inheritance for Israel, blessings for the Gentiles, and fulfillment of covenants.

l: priestcrafts, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Priestcrafts are preaching for money and praise, setting oneself as a light while neglecting Zion’s welfare; they are forbidden by the Lord.

l: miracles, The Second Book of Nephi
s: are_denied denied [by those who say the Lord is no longer a God of miracles] Some teach that the Lord is no longer a God of miracles and that people should not believe in miracles wrought by His hand. This teaching is condemned as a denial of the power of God.

l: dispersion of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi
s: occurs_among the nations [after destruction, famine, pestilence, and bloodshed] Those of the Jews who are not destroyed will be scattered among all nations. Their long dispersion will end when they believe in Christ and are gathered from the isles of the sea and the four parts of the earth.

l: the secret works of darkness, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_chosen_over light [by those who yield unto the devil] Works of darkness are chosen over light by those who yield to the devil. They are associated with secret combinations and lead people to destruction.

l: abominations, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The people’s abominations contribute to the day when the sealed things are withheld from them. The nations, Gentiles, and Jews are drunken with all manner of abominations.

l: people (Nephi's people), The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_a house of Israel Nephi’s people have difficulty understanding the manner of the Jews, and Nephi teaches them plainly so they cannot err. They believe in Christ, keep the law of Moses because of the commandments, and teach their children about Christ.

l: plan of deliverance from death, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_a plan [great and eternal] Nephi delights in God’s grace, justice, power, and mercy in the great and eternal plan of deliverance from death.

l: Judah, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Judah is a fallen, ruined place with men whose tongues and deeds oppose the Lord. Its support, resources, and leaders are taken away; though called the Lord of Hosts’ pleasant plant, it yields oppression and cries, then is overflowed by the king of Assyria.

l: the mountain of the Lord’s house, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The mountain of the Lord’s house is established above mountains and hills in the last days, drawing many people to learn the God of Jacob’s ways.

l: people, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Many people go to the mountain of the Lord’s house to learn his ways and walk in his paths, while the proud are humbled on the day of the Lord.

l: the law, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_sealed sealed [among the disciples] The law is to be sealed among the Lord’s disciples. Those who do not speak according to the law and the testimony have no light in them.

l: war, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_not_learned any more [by nations] War will end when nations beat their swords into plow-shares and their spears into pruning-hooks. Nations will not lift up swords against one another or learn war any more.

l: house of Jacob, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The house of Jacob is a group called to walk in the light of the Lord, yet forsaken after going astray and filling its land with riches, horses, chariots, and idols. Hidden from the Lord, it nevertheless has a remnant that escapes and returns, relying truly on the Lord rather than on him that smote them. Strangers join it, and it possesses former possessors and rules its oppressors. Its ending is redemption: Jacob is no longer ashamed, and its children sanctify the Holy One of Jacob and fear the God of Israel.

l: man, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Man worships idols made by his own hands, but lofty looks and haughtiness are humbled and idols cast away in the day of the Lord. Though breath is in his nostrils and reliance on him is rejected, he becomes more precious than fine gold and Ophir’s golden wedge.

l: the wicked, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The wicked perish and receive the reward of their hands. Because they cast out and kill prophets and saints, they face destruction, fire, thunderings, lightnings, earthquakes, other calamities, and are consumed as stubble.

l: day of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The day of the Lord is near and comes upon nations and everything high, proud, or lifted up, including mountains, towers, ships, and pleasant pictures. It humbles human loftiness, utterly abolishes idols, and makes people hide in fear of the Lord’s majesty. Cruel with wrath and fierce anger, it comes as destruction, bringing sorrow, darkness, punishment, desolation, and the destruction of the wicked.

l: Lord of Hosts, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Lord of Hosts is the Lord who rules, judges, and acts among Jerusalem, Judah, Israel, Jacob, Mount Zion, the vineyard, and the nations. He takes away bread, water, leaders, and skilled people from Jerusalem and Judah, gives children as princes, and stands to plead and judge the people. He enters judgment with the ancients and princes, condemning oppression and their treatment of the poor; he also smites and exposes the daughters of Zion and takes away their ornaments. He looks for judgment and righteousness but finds oppression and cry. As the one who plants and tends the vineyard, he finds wild grapes, destroys its hedge and wall, withholds rain, and lays it waste. High and lifted up on his throne, with a train filling the temple and glory filling the earth, he calls and commissions a speaker while declaring continuing desolation and removal until a tenth returns. He is sanctuary, but also stone of stumbling, rock of offense, gin, and snare. Dwelling in Mount Zion, he has zeal, sends his word to Jacob, judges Israel, and keeps his anger and stretched-out hand. Finally, he commands sanctified and mighty ones, musters battle hosts, shakes heavens and earth in fierce anger, and visits nations with destructive signs, bringing wrongdoers to naught.

l: the people, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The people are oppressed by one another and their neighbors, ruled by children and women, and misled by leaders who destroy their paths. Ancients and princes have consumed their vineyard and keep the poor’s spoil in their houses.

l: the daughters of Zion, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The daughters of Zion are a haughty group marked by stretched-forth necks, wanton eyes, tinkling feet, and many ornaments. The Lord smites their heads, exposes secret parts, and removes their beauty; afterward, the Lord washes away their filth.

l: children, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Children are given as princes and rule, behaving proudly against the ancient as oppressors of the people.

l: women, The Second Book of Nephi
s: rule_over the people Women rule over the people. Their rule is included among the conditions under which the people are led into error.

l: oppression, The Second Book of Nephi
s: affects the people [one by another and by every neighbor] Oppression occurs as every person is against another and every person against his neighbor. The people are also oppressed by children.

l: ruin, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Ruin affects Jerusalem and Judah; a man refuses rule, and Jerusalem is ultimately left desolate.

l: the vineyard, The Second Book of Nephi
s: A vineyard on a fruitful hill is fenced, cleared, planted with choicest vine, and equipped with tower and wine-press. Though expected to yield grapes, it produces wild grapes; its hedge and wall are removed, it is laid waste, and receives neither pruning nor rain.

l: seven women, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Seven women take hold of one man, offering their own bread and apparel while asking to bear his name and remove reproach.

l: one man, The Second Book of Nephi
s: has_name_used_by seven women [to take away their reproach] One man is taken hold of by seven women, who ask to be called by his name.

l: branch of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi
s: A beautiful, glorious branch of the Lord will be beautiful and glorious in that day.

l: escaped of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_a escaped people The escaped of Israel will regard the fruit of the earth as excellent and comely.

l: remnant in Zion and Jerusalem, The Second Book of Nephi
s: A holy remnant in Zion and Jerusalem is called holy and includes each person written among the living.

l: cloud and smoke, The Second Book of Nephi
s: A cloud and smoke will cover every dwelling-place of mount Zion and its assemblies by day as a defence.

l: flaming fire, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_a fire [by night upon every dwelling-place of mount Zion and upon her assemblies] A flaming fire will shine by night upon every dwelling-place of mount Zion and its assemblies as a defence.

l: glory of Zion, The Second Book of Nephi
s: has defence [upon all the glory of Zion] The glory of Zion will have a defence over it.

l: tabernacle, The Second Book of Nephi
s: A tabernacle provides daytime shade, refuge, and cover from heat, storm, and rain.

l: well-beloved, The Second Book of Nephi
s: owns vineyard The well-beloved has a vineyard in a very fruitful hill.

l: men of Judah, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_a pleasant plant [of the Lord of Hosts] The men of Judah are identified as the pleasant plant of the Lord of Hosts. The Lord of Hosts looks for righteousness from them but finds a cry.

l: judgment, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Judgment is what the Lord of Hosts looks for from the house of Israel, but oppression is found instead. The Lord of Hosts shall be exalted in judgment.

l: oppression, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Oppression is found where the Lord of Hosts looks for judgment from the house of Israel.

l: captivity, The Second Book of Nephi
s: receives people [because they have no knowledge] The people go into captivity because they have no knowledge.

l: good, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_called evil [by the condemned] Good is called evil by those under condemnation.

l: law of the Lord of Hosts, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_cast_away cast away [by the condemned] The law of the Lord of Hosts is cast away by those whose root becomes rottenness and whose blossoms go up as dust.

l: anger of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The anger of the Lord is kindled against his people because of transgression and remains unturned despite punishment, with his hand stretched forth amid devastation.

l: land, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The land is darkened by the Lord of Hosts’ wrath and consumed by sorrow and fire, ending utterly desolate as cities and houses stand without inhabitants.

l: the speaker (the narrator), The Second Book of Nephi
s: A man of unclean lips dwelling among unclean people sees the Lord of Hosts as King on a high throne, is purged by a live coal, and answers the Lord’s call: “Here am I; send me.”

l: seraphim, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Celestial beings with six wings stand above the Lord of Hosts, proclaim holiness, then one uses a live coal to purge the speaker’s iniquity and sin.

l: temple, The Second Book of Nephi
s: contains throne The temple is filled by the train of the Lord of Hosts. Its doorposts move at the voice of the seraph who cries, and the house is filled with smoke.

l: people of unclean lips, The Second Book of Nephi
s: has_attribute unclean lips The people of unclean lips are the people among whom the speaker dwells. They will hear without understanding, see without perceiving, and have their hearts, ears, and eyes made unresponsive lest they be converted and healed.

l: sin, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_opposed_by writing [harshly] Nephi's writing speaks harshly against sin according to the plainness of the truth. He says no one will be angry at those words unless that person is of the spirit of the devil.

l: commission to preach, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Lord gives the narrator a commission to preach, sending him to tell unclean-lipped people they will not understand or perceive.

l: holy seed, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Holy seed is the enduring substance of the returning tenth, compared to teil-tree or oak remnants after leaves are cast.

l: king Ahaz, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Ahaz, king of Judah and son of Jotham of David’s house, faces Rezin and Pekah’s attack; the Lord offers a sign and warns of coming trouble.

l: Rezin, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Rezin, king and head of Syria, joins Pekah against Jerusalem; his fierce anger is likened to a smoking firebrand.

l: Pekah the son of Remaliah, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Pekah, Remaliah’s son and Israel’s king, joins Rezin to attack Jerusalem and plot Judah’s breach and Tabeal’s son’s rule.

l: Immanuel, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Immanuel is the name given to a son born of a virgin. He eats butter and honey while learning to refuse evil and choose good. His land’s breadth is filled by the stretching out of the king of Assyria’s wings.

l: Syria, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Syria is a kingdom led by Rezin from Damascus, confederate with Ephraim and waging war against Jerusalem.

l: Ephraim, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Ephraim, a people among Israel headed by Samaria, joins Syria and Manasseh against Judah and attacks it. It is foretold to be broken within three score and five years; later its envy of Judah departs and their adversity ends.

l: Assyria, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Assyria, associated with its king, brings trouble, overwhelming waters, and the taking of Damascus’s riches and Samaria’s spoil. Its king is summoned in acts against the land’s people, while Assyria lays a burden and yoke upon Zion’s people. In the end, the Lord recovers a remnant from Assyria by a highway.

l: Samaria, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Samaria, an inhabited spoil, is conquered by the Assyrian, who threatens Jerusalem with the same fate.

l: war against Jerusalem, The Second Book of Nephi
s: War in which Rezin and Pekah attack Jerusalem, plan to breach Judah and install Tabeal’s son, but fail to conquer.

l: the counsel against Ahaz, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Evil counsel targets Ahaz: Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah plan to attack Judah and install Tabeal’s son, but it will fail.

l: the sign from the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi
s: A sign from the Lord concerns a virgin conceiving, bearing a child, and naming him Immanuel.

l: the child’s birth, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Immanuel’s birth from a virgin fulfills the announcement, preceding the forsaking of Ahaz’s hated land by its kings.

l: Maher-shalal-hash-baz, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_a son [of the prophetess] Maher-shalal-hash-baz is the subject of the writing and the name given to the prophetess’s son. Before the child can say “My father” and “My mother,” the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria will be taken away before the king of Assyria.

l: the king of Assyria, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The king of Assyria comes against this people in glory like strong waters, passes through Judah, overflows, and reaches to the neck.

l: this people, The Second Book of Nephi
s: This people rejects Shiloah’s gentle waters and rejoices in Rezin and Remaliah’s son, then faces Assyrian threat and warnings against confederacy and fear.

l: the waters of Shiloah, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Shiloah’s softly flowing waters are refused by this people.

l: the houses of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi
s: are_affected_by the Lord of Hosts [as a stone of stumbling and rock of offense] The Lord of Hosts becomes a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense to both houses of Israel.

l: the testimony, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_bound bound [among the disciples] The testimony is to be bound up and sealed among the Lord’s disciples. People are directed to the law and to the testimony when others speak.

l: Mount Zion, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Mount Zion is a mount where the Lord of Hosts dwells and performs his work, including work upon Jerusalem, before punishing the king of Assyria; nations fight against it, but their multitude becomes an unsatisfying empty dream.

l: the Assyrian invasion of Judah, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Assyrian invasion floods Judah to the neck, bringing trouble, darkness, hunger, hardship, and anguish.

l: the child (the promised ruler), The Second Book of Nephi
s: The promised ruler is a child given as a son to the people. Government rests on his shoulder; he is called Wonderful, Counselor, The Mighty God, The Everlasting Father, and The Prince of Peace. His rule is established on David’s throne with judgment and justice forever.

l: government, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Government rests on a child’s shoulder, endlessly increases with peace, and is forever ordered on David’s throne and kingdom through judgment and justice.

l: darkness, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_a condition [of dimness and shadow] Darkness characterizes the land and the people who dwell in the land of the shadow of death. The people in darkness see a great light, but the land is later darkened through the wrath of the Lord of Hosts.

l: light, The Second Book of Nephi
s: A great light shines on people walking in darkness and shadow, as the Lord’s word lights upon Israel.

l: yoke, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Assyrian's yoke burdens Israel, then is taken from its neck and destroyed because of the anointing.

l: Assyrian, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Assyrian is the rod of the Lord's anger, sent with indignation to spoil, prey upon, and tread people down. He intends to destroy many nations, boasts that his princes are kings, and compares conquered places. In the Lord's land he is threatened with leanness and burning, then brought underfoot on the mountains; his yoke and burden depart.

l: remnant of the house of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The remnant of Israel returns in that day, turning from its smiter to rely in truth on the Lord God of Hosts.

l: Assyrian army, The Second Book of Nephi
s: has carriages [laid up at Michmash] The Assyrian army is not named in this unit.

l: anger, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Lord's anger is not turned away, and his hand remains stretched out. His anger is described as being used in sending the Assyrian against a hypocritical nation, and it will cease in a little while when the Assyrian is destroyed.

l: the Lord's work upon Mount Zion and Jerusalem, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Lord will perform his whole work upon Mount Zion and upon Jerusalem before punishing the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria.

l: punishment of Assyria, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Lord will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria and the glory of his high looks. The Lord will send leanness among his fat ones and kindle a burning under his glory.

l: rod of God's anger, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Assyrian is called the rod of the Lord's anger, and the staff in the Assyrian's hand is described as the Lord's indignation.

l: remnant's return, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The remnant of Israel and the remnant of Jacob will return to the mighty God. Though Israel is as the sand of the sea, a remnant will return as the consumption decreed overflows with righteousness.

l: consumption, The Second Book of Nephi
s: A determined consumption, decreed by the Lord God of Hosts, overflows with righteousness throughout all the land.

l: burden, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_taken_away people dwelling in Zion [from their shoulder] In that day the Assyrian's burden will be taken away from Israel's shoulder.

l: Jesse, The Second Book of Nephi
s: A rod comes out of Jesse’s stem, and a branch grows from his roots.

l: the rod and branch from Jesse, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The rod and branch grows out of Jesse and receives the Spirit of the Lord: wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and fear. With quick understanding, it judges the poor righteously, reproves the meek equitably, smites the earth, and slays the wicked. Clothed in righteousness and faithfulness, it is the root of Jesse, an ensign of the people, with glorious rest.

l: knowledge of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The earth becomes full of the knowledge of the Lord as the waters cover the sea.

l: fear of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The rod and branch from Jesse have quick understanding in the fear of the Lord and do not judge by sight or hearing.

l: righteousness, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Righteousness is the girdle of the rod and branch from Jesse’s loins. The rod and branch judge the poor with righteousness.

l: the wicked, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The wicked are punished for iniquity, joined by sinners and others who fall by the sword. They are destroyed from the land and ultimately perish when the Lord God divides the people, by fire or the breath of his lips.

l: the holy mountain, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_free_from_harm the earth [none shall hurt nor destroy] No one hurts or destroys in all the Lord’s holy mountain.

l: the outcasts of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Lord assembles the outcasts of Israel.

l: the dispersed of Judah, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Lord gathers the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

l: the highway, The Second Book of Nephi
s: A highway is made for the Lord’s remnant from Assyria, unfolding like Israel’s exodus from Egypt.

l: the recovery of the remnant, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Lord sets his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the islands of the sea.

l: praise, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Praise is offered to the Lord because his anger has turned away and he has comforted the speaker. People are told to praise the Lord, call upon his name, and declare his doings.

l: Babylon, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Babylon is the glory of kingdoms and the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency. It is overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah, becoming forever uninhabited: neither Arabian tents nor shepherds’ folds remain. Desert beasts, doleful creatures, owls, satyrs, island beasts, and dragons occupy its desolation. Its name, remnant, son, and nephew are cut off; it becomes a possession with pools of water, swept by destruction.

l: kingdoms of nations, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_gathered_for battle [as a tumultuous multitude] The kingdoms of nations gather together in a tumultuous multitude in the mountains. They come from a far country, from the end of heaven, for battle.

l: whole land, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_destroyed_by weapons of his indignation The whole land is targeted for destruction by the weapons of the Lord’s indignation. It will be laid desolate.

l: world, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_punished_for evil The world will be made as a wilderness by the man who oppressed it and destroyed its cities.

l: Medes, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Medes are stirred against Babylon, disregarding silver and gold while mercilessly attacking young men and children.

l: rest, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_given_by the Lord [from sorrow, fear, and hard bondage] The Lord will give rest from sorrow, fear, and the hard bondage in which the people were made to serve. The whole earth will also be at rest and quiet after the oppressor ceases.

l: king of Babylon, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_an_oppressor people The king of Babylon will be the subject of a proverb because the oppressor and the golden city have ceased. He will be brought down to hell, cast out like an abominable branch, and denied burial because he destroyed his land and slew his people.

l: Lucifer, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Lucifer, a man fallen from heaven, seeks to ascend above God and rule from the mount of the congregation. After weakening nations and destroying world and cities, he falls, is brought to the pit, and cast out as an abominable branch.

l: man (Lucifer), The Second Book of Nephi
s: Those who see him will consider him and ask whether he is the man who made the earth tremble, shook kingdoms, made the world a wilderness, destroyed cities, and did not open the house of his prisoners.

l: Palestina, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_dissolved dissolved Palestina is warned not to rejoice because the rod of the one who smote it is broken. It will howl and cry because smoke will come from the north, and its root will be killed with famine.

l: purpose of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Lord’s irrevocable purpose concerns the whole earth, will come to pass, and cannot be disannulled or turned back.

l: God the Father, The Second Book of Nephi
s: God the Father is Father of heaven and earth. He commands repentance and baptism by water in the name of Jesus Christ, gives the Holy Ghost to those baptized, and declares salvation for those who endure to the end. He is witnessed by the baptized willing to keep his commandments and receives prayer in Christ’s name for the welfare of souls.

l: nations, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Nations include Jews and receive God’s word in writing. They face judgments, with other nations scourging and scattering Jews, while the Lord creates, remembers, and speaks to all nations; their written testimonies become witnesses.

l: prophets, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Prophets are cast out, stoned, and slain by the wicked, while those who heed and preserve them will not perish.

l: scriptures written by Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Nephi’s writings are kept for his seed across generations, endure while earth stands, judge nations at the last day, and convince people of the true Messiah.

l: prophecy, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_given_by spirit of prophecy [according to plainness] Prophecy reveals the destruction and restoration of the Jews, the coming and rejection of Jesus Christ, and the preservation of Nephi’s writings. Nephi says his prophecy is plain and that no man can err in understanding it.

l: spirit of prophecy, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The spirit of prophecy makes the words of Isaiah plain to those who possess it. Nephi speaks and prophesies according to the spirit in him.

l: destruction of Jerusalem, The Second Book of Nephi
s: occurs_after resurrection of Jesus Christ [again] Jerusalem is destroyed after the Jews reject and crucify Jesus Christ. Nephi says woe comes upon those who fight against God and the people of his church.

l: rejection of Jesus Christ, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_caused_by iniquity [among the Jews] The Jews reject Jesus Christ because of their iniquities, hardness of heart, and stiffness of necks. Nephi teaches that rejecting Christ also denies the prophets and the law.

l: resurrection of Jesus Christ, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Jesus Christ rises from the dead after three days, bringing healing. Those who believe in his name are saved in the kingdom of God, and the resurrection is followed by his showing himself to Nephi’s people amid signs of his birth, death, and resurrection.

l: remission of sins, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Remission of sins is obtained through Jesus Christ, whom Nephi and his people teach their children to seek; after repentance and baptism by water, it comes by baptism of fire and of the Holy Ghost.

l: Holy Ghost, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Holy Ghost is a Spirit and source of utterance. It descends upon Jesus Christ after baptism in the form of a dove, witnesses God the Father and Jesus Christ, and is received after baptism by water or entering in by the way. It brings baptism of fire, enables speech with the tongue of angels, shows recipients what they should do, and carries spoken words to human hearts. It has no place in hardened hearts; denying its utterance brings condemnation. Precepts of men are acceptable only when given by its power.

l: saints, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Saints are persecuted and slain by the wicked, but the righteous who heed prophets protect them and look forward to Christ are preserved.

l: those who have dwindled in unbelief, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Those who have dwindled in unbelief lack the book, are smitten by the Gentiles, and are destroyed suddenly; yet they are not forgotten, as their words and prayers speak through a written, sealed book.

l: destruction of the wicked, The Second Book of Nephi
s: A great, terrible destruction of the wicked unfolds through thunderings, earthquakes, fire, storms, collapsing buildings, and calamities, ending in hell.

l: the last days, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The last days will include the dwindling and destruction of Nephi’s people, the rise of Gentile pride, many churches, secret combinations, and the bringing forth of written records. The words of the righteous and prayers of the faithful will still be preserved. In the last days, or the days of the Gentiles, the nations of the Gentiles and the Jews become drunken with iniquity and abominations. The Lord then visits them and brings forth the words of the book.

l: secret combinations, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_founded_by the devil [according to the combinations of the devil] Secret combinations are described as existing according to the devil’s combinations. They are associated with murder and works of darkness.

l: pride, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Pride brings destruction to the wicked, causes Gentiles to stumble, and burns the proud who do wickedly. It corrupts and lifts up churches, leads them to rob the poor and persecute the meek, and condemns the wise, learned, and rich who are puffed up.

l: the words of the prophets, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The words of the prophets guide the righteous toward Christ; after Nephi’s people are destroyed, they are written, while faithful prayers are heard by God.

l: the book, The Second Book of Nephi
s: A book containing words of those who have slumbered in the dust and God’s revelation from the world’s beginning to its ending. Sealed by God and hidden from the world, it is delivered to a man, comes forth for the Gentiles, is believed by many, carried to Nephi’s seed, then sealed again unto the Lord.

l: nations, The Second Book of Nephi
s: fight_against Zion The nations of the earth become drunken with iniquity and abominations. Those that fight against Zion and distress her are visited, become as an empty dream, and are ultimately brought to naught or cut off.

l: man who receives the book, The Second Book of Nephi
s: A man receives a book and delivers its unsealed words to another; unable to bring the sealed book, he later receives book and words again.

l: man who reads the words, The Second Book of Nephi
s: reads unsealed words [as commanded by God] The man who reads the words says that he is not learned. The Lord tells him to read the words given to him, not to touch the sealed things, and after obtaining the promised witnesses to seal and hide the book again.

l: three witnesses, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Three witnesses behold the book by God’s power and testify to its truth and the truth of the things within it.

l: sealed words, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The sealed words remain undelivered in the book during the people’s wickedness and abominations. At the Lord’s due time, they are read on house tops by Christ’s power and reveal all things from the foundation of the world to its end.

l: unsealed words, The Second Book of Nephi
s: are_delivered_to learned [for reading] The unsealed words are delivered to another person to be shown to the learned. The man who is not learned is commanded to read the words that the Lord gives him.

l: revelation from God, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The revelation from God in the book extends from the beginning of the world to its ending. The sealed revelation is kept in the book until the Lord’s due time.

l: visitation of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The visitation of the Lord of Hosts comes with thunder, earthquake, great noise, storm, tempest, and devouring fire. It falls upon the nations that are drunken with iniquity and abominations.

l: destruction of nations fighting Zion, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_like dream [a dream of a night vision] The nations fighting Zion and distressing her become as a dream of a night vision, like a hungry or thirsty person who awakens empty or faint. The terrible one, the scorner, and those watching for iniquity are also brought to naught or cut off.

l: reading the book, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Reading the book is given to a man who is not learned after the learned reject it. The words are read by the power of Christ, witnesses are obtained, and the book is then sealed and hidden again.

l: sealing and hiding the book, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The book is sealed so that its revelation is kept until the Lord’s due time. After the man reads the commanded words and obtains the promised witnesses, he seals up the book again and hides it for the Lord to preserve the unread words.

l: churches, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Churches built up without the Lord contend, teach by learning, deny the Holy Ghost and God’s power, and are corrupted by pride, false teachers, and false doctrine. Lifted up, they rob the poor through fine sanctuaries and clothing and persecute the meek and poor in heart.

l: the humble followers of Christ, The Second Book of Nephi
s: are_led led [and err in many instances because taught by precepts of men] The humble followers of Christ are among the few who have not gone astray. Nevertheless, they are led into error in many instances because they are taught by the precepts of men.

l: the seed of the speaker, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The remnant of Nephi’s seed, descendants of the Jews from Jerusalem, will learn their origins and be restored to knowledge of their fathers and Jesus Christ, becoming a pure and delightsome people after many generations.

l: inhabitants of the earth, The Second Book of Nephi
s: perish destruction of the wicked [when fully ripe in iniquity] The inhabitants of the earth will be destroyed when they are fully ripe in iniquity unless they repent of their wickedness and abominations.

l: kingdom of the devil, The Second Book of Nephi
s: must_shake shaking The kingdom of the devil must shake, and those who belong to it must be stirred to repentance or be grasped by the devil's everlasting chains and perish.

l: precepts of men, The Second Book of Nephi
s: teach false doctrines [when not given by the power of the Holy Ghost] Precepts of men lead churches and even the humble followers of Christ into error when they replace the Lord's counsel. They are acceptable only when given by the power of the Holy Ghost.

l: destruction of the wicked, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_avoided_by repentance [of wickedness and abominations] The wicked will perish when they are fully ripe in iniquity, and those who follow false doctrines, commit whoredoms, or pervert the Lord's way will be thrust down to hell. Repentance can avert this destruction.

l: the fall of the great and abominable church, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The great and abominable church’s fall is great: it must tumble to the earth.

l: Nephites, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Nephites are a people who write God’s words, possess records from the Jews and lost tribes of Israel, and share their words with those peoples.

l: lost tribes of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Lost tribes of Israel, led away by the Lord God, write his words; their words join those of the Jews and Nephites.

l: Bible, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Bible proceeds from the Jews, the Lord God's ancient covenant people, yet does not contain all the Lord God's words.

l: gospel of Jesus Christ, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_declared_among remnant of our seed The gospel of Jesus Christ will be declared among the remnant of Nephi’s seed. Through it, they will be restored to knowledge of their fathers and of Jesus Christ.

l: all nations, kindreds, tongues, and people, The Second Book of Nephi
s: have_their_things_made_known known The Lord God will commence his work among all nations, kindreds, tongues, and people to bring about the restoration of his people upon the earth.

l: the great division among the people, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_caused_by Lord God The great division among the people will come speedily when the Lord God separates the wicked from his people. The wicked will be destroyed, while the Lord will spare his people.

l: Satan, The Second Book of Nephi
s: has_power_over the hearts of the children of men [not for a long time] Satan will have power over the hearts of the children of men no more for a long time.

l: beloved brethren, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Nephi addresses his beloved brethren and teaches them about the doctrine of Christ. He urges them to follow Jesus Christ, press forward with steadfastness, and endure to the end. The beloved brethren ponder what they should do after entering in by the way. They are taught to receive the Holy Ghost, feast upon the words of Christ, seek knowledge, and pray.

l: baptism of fire and of the Holy Ghost, The Second Book of Nephi
s: follows baptism by water The baptism of fire and of the Holy Ghost comes after repentance, baptism by water, and witnessing willingness to keep the commandments. It brings a new tongue and the ability to speak with the tongue of angels.

l: straight and narrow path, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The straight and narrow path is the way entered through repentance and baptism by water. It leads to eternal life, requires receiving the Holy Ghost, pressing forward, feasting upon the word of Christ, and continuing until the end of the day of probation.

l: gate, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_a repentance and baptism by water [the way of entry] The gate by which people enter is repentance and baptism by water. After entering through the gate, they receive a remission of their sins by fire and by the Holy Ghost.

l: the doctrine of Christ, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The doctrine of Christ is the only and true doctrine of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost. It unfolds through repentance, baptism by water, entering in by the way, receiving the Holy Ghost, following Jesus Christ, and enduring to the end, until Christ manifests himself in the flesh.

l: words of Christ, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The word of Christ leads people into the way through unshaken faith, teaches all they should do, and must be feasted upon while pressing forward toward eternal life.

l: faith in Christ, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Faith in Christ is unshaken reliance on him to enter the straight and narrow path and wholly upon his merits; Nephi’s great faith leads him to pray and expect spotless souls at Christ’s judgment-seat.

l: enduring to the end, The Second Book of Nephi
s: leads_to eternal life [with steadfastness in Christ and feasting upon the word of Christ] Those who endure to the end by following the example of the Son of the living God shall be saved. Enduring to the end is required after entering the strait and narrow path.

l: men, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Men refuse plainly given knowledge and understanding, prompting Nephi to mourn their unbelief, wickedness, ignorance, and stiffneckedness.

l: prayer, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Prayer must always be offered to the Father in Christ’s name before performing anything unto the Lord, so the performance benefits the soul.

l: words of Christ, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Words of Jesus Christ are given to Nephi, teach souls to do good, and will be shown with power and glory as his at the last day.

l: writing, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Nephi’s writing, esteemed as of great worth, is written in weakness yet will be made strong for readers; it teaches of their fathers and Jesus Christ, persuades souls to do good and believe, and plainly condemns sin.

l: the narrow gate, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_entered_by souls [when reconciled unto Christ] People who are to be reconciled unto Christ must enter into the narrow gate.

l: The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi
s: The Book of Jacob records Jacob’s stewardship of the small plates, which Nephi commanded be used to preserve sacred teaching. Jacob and his brother Joseph are consecrated priests and teachers among the people of Nephi. After Nephi dies and appoints a successor, the people continue calling their kings Nephi. Under the second king, many become proud, seek riches, and practice wickedness. Jacob speaks in the temple, condemning costly apparel, persecution of the poor, misuse of wealth, whoredoms, and plural wives. He teaches that they must have one wife and warns that their conduct has wounded wives and children. He urges the pure in heart to pray in faith and trust God, while warning the unrepentant that their land will be cursed and the Lamanites will scourge them. He says the Lamanites are more righteous concerning marriage and forbids reviling them and committing sin. Jacob explains that the plates preserve knowledge of Christ for later generations. He testifies that Christ’s atonement, resurrection, and glory were known through prophets and fathers before Christ’s coming. He warns against rejecting revelation and prophesies that the Jews will reject the sure foundation, though the stone will become the head of the corner. He includes Zenos’s allegory of the olive-tree: the Lord of the vineyard labors to preserve, nourish, prune, and graft the trees until good fruit is restored; corrupt branches are cast away, and eventually the vineyard is burned. Jacob applies this to the house of Israel, urging repentance, faithfulness to prophets and Christ, entrance through the strait gate, and perseverance toward eternal life. Finally, Sherem denies Christ and challenges Jacob. Jacob confounds him through scripture and the Lord’s power. Sherem seeks a sign, is struck down, confesses that the devil deceived him, and dies. The people return to peace and the love of God, search the scriptures, defend themselves from the Lamanites, and Jacob gives the plates to Enos.

l: Jacob, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi
s: Jacob, Nephi’s brother, is consecrated by Nephi as a priest and teacher and is called as a prophet to declare and diligently teach God’s word to the people of Nephi. Nephi commands him to write precious spiritual teachings on the small plates and preserve them for Christ’s sake and the people. With Joseph, Jacob bears responsibility for teaching, fearing sin if he fails to do so. After Nephi’s death, he speaks in the temple, rebuking crimes, pride, riches, and whoredoms. He comforts the pure in heart, urging faith, prayer, and attention to God’s pleasing word, while calling the people to repent and avoid reviling the Lamanites. Though engraving is difficult, he writes so later children and brethren may know their fathers. He teaches Christ, the atonement, resurrection, revelation, and the sure foundation; worships the Father in Christ’s name; and receives power through grace. He prophesies, calls his brethren to cleave unto God, warns against hardened hearts and rejection of words concerning Christ, and bids farewell before the bar of God.

l: Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi
s: Nephi is king and great protector of the people of Nephi, defending them with the sword of Laban. He commands Jacob about the small plates and sacred preservation, consecrates Jacob and Joseph as priests and teachers, and commands Enos through Jacob. Loved and honored by his people, he appoints a king and ruler, then dies.

l: Christ, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi
s: Christ is the Only Begotten Son, known and spoken of by prophets and testified of in scripture before his coming. Jacob and his people know of him through revelation and prophecy, and Jacob urges all people to believe in him, view his death, bear his cross, and come unto him. His glory is hoped for before his coming; he provides atonement and resurrection power and has a kingdom and doctrine. People are taught to hope in Christ rather than seek riches. Though the Jews may reject him as the foundation stone, Jacob warns against rejecting words concerning him. Sherem denies Christ, then confesses him before the people, while Jacob affirms that he shall come.

l: God, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi
s: God is the Creator of heaven, earth, and all flesh, creating by the power of his word so that people keep his commandments and glorify him forever. God possesses goodness, mercy, justice, wrath, and power over heaven and earth. He commands his word to be declared, condemns pride, whoredoms, and abominations, and values every person as precious. He consoles and pleads for the pure in heart while sending justice against those who seek their destruction; he also shows mercy to those who observe his commandments. God reveals mysteries and his ways, gives or removes plainness according to people’s desires, and shows weakness so people recognize that power comes by his grace. He remembers the house of Israel and extends mercy all day long to those who will not harden their hearts. Finally, he pours his Spirit into Jacob, empowers him against Sherem, answers his prayer, and manifests power among the multitude.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi
s: The people of Nephi are descendants and followers of Nephi, whose history is engraven on his other plates and who are protected by him. Jacob and Joseph teach them and seek to persuade them to come unto Christ. Under the second king, they grow hard-hearted, seek gold, silver, and precious ores, become proud, wear costly apparel, and persecute brethren. Though commanded to have one wife and no whoredoms, they labor in sin, break commandments, and grieve their wives and children. They are warned to repent, remember their children, avoid reviling the Lamanites, and abandon fornication and every kind of sin. After Sherem's death, they search the scriptures, reject his words, have peace and restoration, fortify against the Lamanites, trust God, and conquer their enemies.

l: Nephites, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi
s: Nephites are people friendly to Nephi, also called the people of Nephi; the term includes Jacobites, Josephites, Zoramites, and those not Lamanites, identified by kings’ reigns.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi
s: The Lamanites are a people and brethren of the people of Nephi, named by Jacob for those who seek to destroy the people of Nephi rather than by former family names. Though marked by unbelief, hatred, inherited filthiness, and a sore cursing, they are described as more righteous than the people of Nephi in observing the commandment concerning marriage: husbands, wives, and children love one another. Because of this observance, God does not destroy them, and they shall one day become a blessed people. Yet they delight in war and bloodshed, hold eternal hatred, and continually seek to destroy the people of Nephi; efforts to restore them to truth are vain.

l: house of Israel, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi
s: The house of Israel is a stiffnecked, gainsaying people likened to a tame olive-tree: nourished and planted, then pruned, grafted, scattered, and ultimately gathered as natural fruit is restored. The Lord remembers roots and branches and saves those who do not harden their hearts.

l: temple, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi
s: is_a place of teaching [Jacob teaches the people there] Jacob teaches the people in the temple after obtaining his errand from the Lord.

l: small plates, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi
s: Small plates hold precious things and sacred records: preaching, revelation, and prophecy. Nephi commands Jacob to write and preserve them, then hand them down to his seed.

l: doctrine of Christ, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi
s: The doctrine of Christ is good, preached by Jacob, and opposed by a man and Sherem, who seek to overthrow it by declaring there should be no Christ; Jacob confounds Sherem.

l: Christ’s kingdom, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi
s: is_to_come future Jacob and his people learn of Christ’s kingdom through revelations and the spirit of prophecy.

l: word of God, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi
s: The word of God is taught diligently to the people of Nephi by Jacob and Joseph. It is plain, pleasing, and heals the wounded soul, yet it also exposes wickedness and pierces minds through admonition. Jacob declares it by God’s command, and the pure in heart are invited to receive and feast upon it and God’s love.

l: faith, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi
s: becomes unshaken [through witnesses] Faith becomes unshaken through searching the prophets, receiving revelations, and having the spirit of prophecy. Faith in Christ is included among the conditions for obtaining resurrection and hope of glory.

l: sin, The Book of Jacob, the Brother of Nephi
s: Sin is the people’s wrongdoing, for which Jacob and Joseph bear responsibility if they fail to teach God’s word diligently. It begins as labor in sin, pride, persecution, and sexual wrongdoing, then Jacob warns the people of Nephi against fornication and lasciviousness, whose sins may be heaped upon them at the last day.
